title: Behavioral Transition Protocol in Mice Facing Uncontrollable Experiences
author: Li, Zhang, et al.
materials: Coulbourn H03-04 Habitest Linc output converter

steps.title: Prepare exposure apparatus
steps.instruction: Set up two separate uncontrollable experience apparatuses: (i) an inescapable electrical foot‑shock chamber (IS model) and (ii) an inescapable discontinuous swimming tank (IDS model). Ensure each apparatus can deliver the stimulus without allowing the mouse to escape.

steps.title: Run exposure sessions
steps.instruction: Expose each mouse to three sessions per model, each session lasting 1 hour, with one session per day. Each 1‑hour session consists of 60 trials of uncontrollable experiences (foot shock for IS, swimming for IDS).

substeps.instruction: For the IS model, deliver inescapable electrical foot shocks in 60 trials per session.
For the IDS model, place the mouse in the swimming tank for 60 discontinuous swimming trials per session.

steps.title: Video‑record each session
steps.instruction: Videotape the entire 1‑hour session for both IS and IDS models, capturing the mouse behavior during each foot‑shock or swimming interval for later analysis.

steps.title: Classify trial behavior
steps.instruction: Review the videos and, for every trial, assign the mouse’s behavior as either “action” (e.g., escape‑like response) or “no‑action” (e.g., passive behavior). Record the classification for all 60 trials of each session.

steps.title: Create binary codes
steps.instruction: Convert the action/no‑action classifications into three binary series per mouse:

substeps.instruction: Generate “Action Value”: assign 1 if the trial is action, 0 otherwise.
Generate “No‑Action Value”: assign 1 if the trial is no‑action, 0 otherwise.
Compute “Transition Value” for each trial as Transition Value = Action Value – No‑Action Value (resulting in 1 for action, –1 for no‑action).

steps.title: Fit exponential learning model
steps.instruction: Using GraphPad Prism (or any equivalent software), fit the Transition Values to the exponential learning equation (Equation 4): Pₙ = –1 + 2 e^{α n}, where n is trial number and α is the transition‑rate coefficient. Obtain the best‑fit line and record the α value for each mouse.

substeps.instruction: Enter the trial number (n) and corresponding Transition Value into the software.
Select Equation 4 (Pₙ = –1 + 2 e^{α n}) as the fitting model.
Run the fit and extract the α (transition rate) for each individual mouse.

steps.title: Statistical analysis of α values
steps.instruction: Analyze the α values across experimental groups:

substeps.instruction: Test normality of α distributions with the Shapiro‑Wilk test.
If data are normally distributed, compare groups using an unpaired Student’s t‑test.
If data are not normally distributed, compare groups using an unpaired Mann‑Whitney test.
